These high-level officials regularly gather to coordinate policies and address pressing international financial and economic issues. The G20 was formed in 1999 in response to financial crises of the late 1990s, aiming to bring together systemically important industrialized and developing economies to discuss key issues in the global economy.

Key topics expected to be on the agenda include persistent inflation, strategies for fostering sustainable economic growth, and managing global debt levels, especially in developing countries. Central bank governors, responsible for monetary policy, and finance ministers, who oversee fiscal policy, play vital roles in shaping their respective national economies. Their collective discussions at the G20 are essential for developing coordinated responses to shared challenges.
